evals.name: loader-page-to-region-composition
evals.prompt: Review this Next.js App Router route architecture. The page at app/dashboard/page.tsx is async, fetches user, metrics, notifications, and marketing recommendations at the top, then passes all results through props into child components. Only auth must block the route; the other regions can load independently. Recommend a refactor using React Server Components, Suspense, skeletons, and scoped error handling without replacing the project's existing data layer.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the route as a loader-style async page, keeps only auth/gating at route level, moves region-specific reads into async Server Components, adds meaningful Suspense boundaries with colocated skeletons, scopes errors by region, and preserves existing data tooling.
expectations: Uses the strict eight-section output contract or explicitly marks empty sections as Not applicable.
Recommends a synchronous route compositor unless route-level auth/gating requires async work.
Moves metrics, notifications, and recommendations reads into owning async Server Component regions.
Adds meaningful Suspense boundaries and colocated shape-matched skeletons for independently streaming regions.
Does not recommend making the whole route a Client Component or replacing the existing data layer by default.

evals.name: next15-params-thenable-sync-shell
evals.prompt: We are on Next.js 15. In app/products/[slug]/page.tsx, params is typed as Promise<{ slug: string }>. The current page is async only to await params and then fetch product, reviews, and related products before rendering. How should we restructure it so the page remains a composition shell while product regions own their data? Include guidance for params/searchParams promises.
evals.expected_output: Uses Next.js 15 thenable route prop guidance, considers params.then(...) to derive slug promises without making the page a loader, passes minimal typed promises/IDs to async regions, and separates independently loading product/reviews/related regions behind Suspense where appropriate.
expectations: Explicitly notes Next.js 15 params/searchParams can be promise-like and should be typed accordingly.
Considers params.then(...) as a way to keep the page synchronous.
Avoids centralizing product, reviews, and related-products fetching in the page when regions can own reads.
Keeps props minimal and serializable across server/client boundaries.
Includes version notes rather than assuming sync params.

evals.name: preserve-intentional-client-cache
evals.prompt: A Next.js App Router analytics page uses TanStack Query in a Client Component for live filters, polling, user-triggered refresh, and optimistic edits. Another agent suggested deleting React Query because Server Components can fetch on the server. Review the architecture and recommend what should stay client-managed versus what could move to server-rendered RSC regions.
evals.expected_output: Rejects RSC absolutism, preserves intentional TanStack Query usage for live/user-driven/polling/optimistic flows, identifies any server-renderable static initial regions separately, and keeps client leaves/wrappers focused on interactivity.
expectations: Preserves TanStack Query where it supports live, user-driven, polling, or optimistic UX.
Does not claim React Query/TanStack Query is obsolete because RSC exists.
Separates server-renderable initial/static reads from intentionally client-managed data.
Recommends Client Components as leaves or wrappers instead of promoting unrelated regions to client rendering.
Mentions cache invalidation or mutation strategy should follow project conventions.

evals.name: overgrown-client-component-leaf-extraction
evals.prompt: In app/settings/page.tsx the entire settings page has 'use client' because one nested SaveButton uses click handlers and useOptimistic. The page also imports server-only account and billing helpers indirectly. Recommend a safer RSC architecture with Server Components and a client leaf while preserving optimistic UX.
evals.expected_output: Identifies client boundary creep, moves server reads back to Server Components, extracts the interactive SaveButton/form behavior into a Client Component leaf, keeps props serializable/minimal, uses Server Functions/actions where supported, and preserves useOptimistic for immediate feedback.
expectations: Flags the whole-page 'use client' as client boundary creep.
Moves account and billing server reads into Server Components or server helpers, not Client Components.
Extracts the interactive SaveButton/form behavior into a small Client Component leaf or wrapper.
Keeps optimistic UX with useOptimistic or an equivalent project-standard pattern.
Warns against server-only imports crossing into Client Components.

evals.name: cache-dedupe-not-batching
evals.prompt: Review a route where an async Server Component renders 80 ProductCard components. Each ProductCard calls getProduct(id), wrapped in React cache(). The team believes cache() batches the product lookups. Explain the architectural problem and recommend an RSC-friendly data ownership and loading plan.
evals.expected_output: Explains that React cache() dedupes identical calls but does not batch many distinct IDs, recommends bulk reads/joins/dataloaders/API batching/precomputed read models for many IDs, and keeps RSC ownership/loading boundaries meaningful without creating waterfalls.
expectations: States that React cache() dedupes identical calls within a request scope but does not batch different IDs.
Recommends batching, bulk reads, joins, dataloaders, API batching, or precomputed read models for many distinct IDs.
Considers whether the product list region should own a bulk read rather than each card causing N+1 reads.
Does not suggest Suspense micro-boundaries around every tiny ProductCard by default.
Includes validation steps for query count, waterfall behavior, or performance impact.

evals.name: next16-cachecomponents-static-shell
evals.prompt: We are upgrading to Next.js 16 with cacheComponents. A marketing route has a mostly static shell, but a personalized recommendations panel reads cookies and user-specific data. The current implementation awaits the personalized read in page.tsx before rendering anything. Recommend a page composition that preserves the static shell and gives the dynamic panel a good loading and error experience.
evals.expected_output: Checks Next.js 16/cacheComponents implications, keeps the static shell synchronous when possible, moves personalized dynamic reads into an async region behind meaningful Suspense, adds colocated skeleton/error handling, and avoids unscoped dynamic reads that make the whole route dynamic unless intended.
expectations: Explicitly discusses Next.js 16 cacheComponents/static shell versus dynamic region implications.
Recommends preserving the static shell instead of blocking it on personalized data.
Moves cookie/user-specific recommendations into an async Server Component region behind Suspense.
Adds a region-specific skeleton and scoped error/recovery behavior for the personalized panel.
Warns against one unscoped dynamic read pulling the whole route into dynamic rendering unless intended.

evals.name: swr-catalog-category-client-cache-preservation
evals.prompt: Review app/catalog/[category] in a Next.js App Router fixture. params is typed as Promise<{ category: string }>. The route has server-owned catalog product regions and an InventoryBadgeClient that imports useSWR from swr, calls useSWR(`/api/inventory?category=${category}`, fetchInventory, { revalidateOnFocus: false }), supports browser refresh/filter state, and renders inventory cache status. Unknown categories should call notFound(). Another agent wants to replace the SWR leaf with a Server Component fetch because RSC can fetch data. Recommend the architecture.
evals.expected_output: Preserves the intentional SWR client cache leaf, keeps the route shell server-rendered and not route-wide client, handles promise params and category notFound with minimal blocking, keeps server-owned catalog reads in async regions, and provides evidence/validation for boundaries, cache ownership, and not-found behavior.
expectations: Explicitly preserves SWR for browser-owned cache behavior such as refresh, focus/refetch, filters, validation state, or shared client cache.
Does not replace the SWR leaf with a Server Component read unless the user intentionally removes browser-owned behavior.
Keeps 'use client' limited to the inventory/cache leaf or wrapper, not the whole route.
Handles Promise-shaped params and category notFound without centralizing all region reads in page.tsx.
Maps server-owned catalog reads to owning async Server Component regions with Suspense and failure recovery.
Includes concrete evidence and validation checks for SWR preservation, route boundaries, notFound, and e2e behavior.

evals.name: next16-cache-directives-marketing-copy
evals.prompt: A Next.js 16 app has cacheComponents: true. app/marketing has a static hero copy helper and a separate uncached pricing/personalization region. The team wants to use 'use cache', cacheTag('marketing-hero-copy'), and cacheLife('hours'), but is also passing user/request data through nearby regions. Review the architecture and recommend where cache directives belong.
evals.expected_output: Checks cacheComponents before recommending cache directives, puts 'use cache', cacheTag, and cacheLife only inside the genuinely cacheable server helper/component, keeps request-specific or personalized reads outside the cached scope behind Suspense, and avoids decorative or unsafe caching.
expectations: Verifies or asks to verify cacheComponents: true before relying on Next.js 16 cache directives.
Imports cacheLife/cacheTag from next/cache and places them inside a cached server scope with 'use cache'.
Keeps cookies, request-specific values, runtime promises, and browser-owned filters out of shared cached scopes.
Preserves a static shell while isolating uncached dynamic regions behind meaningful Suspense and recovery UI.
Does not conflate React cache() request dedupe with Next.js cache directives or batching.

evals.name: nested-error-domains-and-evidence
evals.prompt: A dashboard/analytics route has independent summary, chart, notifications, and recommendations regions. The fixture exposes SCENARIO_FAIL_REGION, SCENARIO_SLOW_REGION, SCENARIO_FORCE_NOT_FOUND, and SCENARIO_LATENCY_MS. The current refactor adds a single route-level error.tsx and a generic loading.tsx but no local Suspense, scoped fallbacks, or proof that one region failure leaves the rest of the route usable. Review the topology and required evidence.
evals.expected_output: Requires meaningful local Suspense and scoped recovery for independent regions, distinguishes route identity notFound from recoverable region failures, preserves static shell content during slow regions, and demands concrete validation evidence such as tests, traces, screenshots, or route-event logs.
expectations: Rejects a single all-page fallback/error boundary as sufficient for independently failing regions.
Pairs each independently slow region with a shape-matched fallback and scoped failure behavior.
Distinguishes notFound/redirect/auth route gates from optional region error recovery.
Preserves shell and unrelated regions when one region is slow or fails.
Asks for concrete evidence: validation commands, Playwright traces/screenshots, route-event logs, or targeted e2e assertions.
